question: How does methane tetra-p-phenylphosphonic acid coordinate with Cu(II) ions to form one-dimensional and two-dimensional frameworks?
answer: Methane tetra-p-phenylphosphonic acid coordinates with Cu(II) ions through its phosphonate ends to form one-dimensional and two-dimensional frameworks. In one-dimensional structures, single phosphonate oxygen arms from MTPPA-H6 and MTPPA-H5 ligands coordinate to the square pyramidal {Cu(terpy)}2+ building units, resulting in zigzag chains. For two-dimensional frameworks, the MTPPA-H4 ligand, with distinct phosphonate ends including fully protonated, fully deprotonated, and half-protonated units, interacts with both {Cu(terpy)}2+ and {Cu2(pbterpy)}4+ building units. The incorporation of a second Cu(II) ion from {Cu2(pbterpy)}4+ extends the one-dimensional chains into two-dimensional networks. These frameworks exhibit void spaces and predictable structural connectivity driven by the coordination angles and deprotonation states of the MTPPA ligand.

The paper explores the synthesis of metal-organic complexes using a novel ligand, methane tetra-p-phenylphosphonic acid (MTPPA), with Cu(II) ions. It focuses on the use of MTPPA as a bridging ligand in hydrothermal and solvothermal reactions to form one-dimensional and two-dimensional structures, characterized using single-crystal X-ray diffraction and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
